subject: Subprocessor egress retention & TIA sampling instructions for MedTech Works audit
messages:
From: Sara Linden <sara.linden@medtech-works.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood-inference.com
Cc: compliance@medtech-works.com, procurement@medtech-works.com
Date: Sat, 24 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request — retention windows and egress logs

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. As part of our upcoming regulatory audit (US & UK clinics), our auditors have asked for: a) proof of how Redwood captures subprocessor egress events, b) retention windows for those logs, and c) a sampling plan that shows how you will provide TIA-level evidence for a subset of customer-controlled datasets.

Can you share a short runbook or walk-through that outlines:
- which subprocessors generate egress logs (by function),
- where those logs are stored and how long they are retained,
- the proposed sampling methodology (number of samples, selection heuristics, timebox), and
- any on-demand export or escrow options we can use for auditors.

We aim to include this in the audit packet by the end of next week. I attached a blank evidence matrix for you to populate if that helps.

Appreciate it — Sara

[Sara Linden | Compliance Lead, MedTech Works]
From: tessa_morgan@redwood-inference.com
To: Sara Linden <sara.linden@medtech-works.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com
Date: Sat, 24 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — retention windows and egress logs

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise TIA sampling brief and our current subprocessor roster. Quick notes up top:

- Egress events: captured at both the serving runtime (request/response metadata) and at subprocessor interfaces (S3 transfers, logging agents). We have correlatable request IDs across layers.
- Retention: metadata + access logs retained 13 months by default; detailed packet-level logs kept 90 days. There are longer-term export/escrow options for audit customers (see attachment).
- Sampling: propose a 20-sample plan covering 2 months of traffic, stratified by region and model variant. Selection uses request-id hashing + time windows to avoid bias.

I'm looping in Marissa and Kim for the legal/DPAs and for an attachment that maps DPA clauses to the evidence items. If that plan works, we can produce an evidence packet and a signed attestation within 72 hours.

Attachments: medtech_evidence_matrix.xlsx; redwood-subprocessor-list-202806.xlsx; tia-sample-criteria.pdf

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood-inference.com, Sara Linden <sara.linden@medtech-works.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com, jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com
Date: Sun, 25 Jun 2028 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — retention windows and egress logs

Sara / Tessa — quick legal read and clarifications from the DPA perspective.

1) UK IDTA / SCCs: the evidence we produce will be tied to the legal flow documented in the DPA and the UK Addendum when applicable. For MedTech Works (processing UK patient data), we will include the IDTA addendum snapshot and a redline summary mapping each evidence item to the relevant clause (e.g., logging retention -> Section 4.2).

2) Subprocessor controls: the subprocessor sheet indicates where we rely on partners (cloud storage, telemetry ingestion). For subprocessors outside the EEA/UK, we will also provide our contractual flow (DBA + SCC clause reference) and the TIA sampling will explicitly include at least one flow routed through a non-UK/EEA subprocess to demonstrate fallback safeguards.

3) Evidence pedigree & attestations: legal can sign an attestation that the artifacts provided are generated from production telemetry; however, for escrow-style exports we need procurement confirmation on scope (full vs sampled export).

Action items:
- Kimberly: draft the attestation language aligned with DPA clauses (target: tomorrow EOD).
- Tessa: produce the 20-sample list and populate the evidence matrix (target: Tue 26 Jun 12:00 PT).
- Jonas: confirm whether infra can run a protected export job for 7-day window if procurement requests it (jonas, pls advise).

Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy & Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, tessa_morgan@redwood-inference.com, Sara Linden <sara.linden@medtech-works.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jun 2028 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — retention windows and egress logs

All,

Draft attestation below — feel free to comment inline.

---ATTACHMENT: attestation-draft.txt---
Redwood Inference attests that the artifacts contained in the attached evidence packet are derived from production telemetry for the time windows listed. Artifacts include request/response metadata, storage transfer logs, and subprocessor ingress/egress records. Retention windows, access controls, and retention policy references are provided for each artifact.

This attestation is provided pursuant to the DPA and the related UK Addendum (if applicable) and is limited to the scope defined by the requestor. Redwood does not disclose customer content unless compelled by lawful process or as otherwise required under contract.
---END ATTACHMENT---

I also confirmed with infra that on-demand protected exports are supported for compliance customers; execution requires a signed export scope form and a scheduled maintenance window (to limit performance impact). Jonas, can you confirm the shortest lead time?

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com, tessa_morgan@redwood-inference.com, marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, Sara Linden <sara.linden@medtech-works.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jun 2028 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — retention windows and egress logs

Kim / team — operational update:

- Shortest lead time for a protected export job is 72 hours from signed export scope receipt. We can stage an extract for a 7-day window; for larger windows we recommend the sampling approach to keep operator load low.
- Exports are hashed and access-controlled; we will produce checksums and an audit log of who pulled the artifact. An infra engineer will supervise the export and produce the chain-of-custody note.
- For the proposed 20-sample TIA plan: infra can run the selection job using the request-id hashing approach described by Tessa; we will produce the raw logs and a redacted packet that removes other customers' identifiers.

Next steps: Tessa to send the sample list by Tue 12:00 PT; Procurement (MedTech) to confirm whether they want a single 7-day protected export or the stratified sample only. Once we have that, infra schedules the job (72h).

Jonas Weber
Director, Infrastructure Reliability
Redwood Inference
